A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ELFS and retain the same central framework. All 16 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original coreset-selection experiments on five vision datasets, alongside encoder ablations, transferability tests, pseudo-label analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments on four vision datasets, component ablations, transferability tests, and a new class-incremental continual-learning evaluation in Appendix C.6.

M1.justification: The TEMI pseudo-labeling, training-dynamics scoring, and double-end pruning pipeline remains intact. A limited procedural revision concerns beta selection: v1's Limitations state that the implementation uses binary search, whereas v2 describes and times grid search in Section 4.3.2 and Appendix D.

E1.justification: CINIC10 evaluation is removed, while CIFAR10, CIFAR100, STL10, and ImageNet-1K remain. V2 adds class-incremental continual learning on CIFAR10 and a scenario without public pretrained encoders, using self-supervised training on the target unlabeled dataset. These introduce substantive task and resource-condition coverage beyond the retained classification benchmarks.

E2.justification: V2 adds FreeSel to the benchmark comparisons. Its CIFAR100 sampling ablation evaluates D2 with pseudo-label difficulty scores, replacing the uniform-score label-free D2 row in v1's corresponding comparison (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 3). Conversely, v1 Table 3's DINO-based Prototypicality and uniform-score D2 comparisons disappear. The evaluated comparator configurations therefore change materially.

E3.justification: V2 specifies AUM for the main experiments, whereas v1 identifies key CIFAR experiments as forgetting-score based; some reported beta settings also change between v1 Table 7 and v2 Table 9. New protocols include self-supervised encoder training and five-stage continual learning with two incoming classes per stage and 10%, 20%, or 30% storage budgets. Core benchmark training schedules and the 90/10 beta-selection split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds controlled comparisons of TEMI, SCAN, and K-means; AUM, forgetting, and EL2N; and public versus self-trained encoders. It also adds ImageNet architecture transfer, hard/easy-example training trajectories, and an ELFS-versus-random difficulty-distribution analysis. Existing CLIP encoder results are revised and moved, while CLIP class-wise error plots and the detailed runtime analysis are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The additional tables and plots in v2 continue to present point results without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive FreeSel, clustering, scoring, self-trained-encoder, transfer, and continual-learning results, while removing CINIC10 and per-stage runtime results. Main CIFAR10/DINO accuracy at 90% pruning changes from 86.9% to 87.3%, accompanying the reported scoring change rather than establishing a matched-setting gain. The ImageNet DINO accuracy sequence is retained from v1 Table 8 in v2 Table 1.

T1.justification: V1's explicit O(log n) complexity assertion for binary beta search is removed; v2 instead offers a qualitative early-stopping suggestion in Appendix D. The optimization problem, TEMI objective, and pseudo-label aggregation equations remain unchanged. V2's standard AUM formula explains an existing metric, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions—label-free training-dynamics estimation and double-end pruning—remain unchanged. V2 qualifies the headline baseline comparison by requiring the same encoder, changes the claimed benchmark scope from five datasets to four, and emphasizes ImageNet comparisons. Claims of outperforming label-free methods and sometimes matching supervised selection persist.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion: self-trained encoders address v1's pretrained-model limitation, Appendix C.5 explains the advantage over random sampling through difficulty coverage, and Appendix C.6 argues for reusable coresets in continual learning versus semi-supervised learning. Appendix D also reframes beta-search overhead as feasible and adds mislabeled-example removal as a rationale for pruning hard data.

D1.justification: Most optimizer, training-budget, clustering-head, and nearest-neighbor details are retained. V2 replaces a future code-release promise with a stated available implementation and repository address, and reports approximately 17 hours on four A6000 GPUs for an ImageNet beta search. It removes v1's per-stage runtime table, associated 2080 Ti/server details, and codebase licensing disclosure, while updating the beta table.

R1.justification: V2 adds FreeSel and literature supporting its semi-supervised-learning, continual-learning, and architecture-search discussion, while retaining the central positioning against geometry-based selection. It removes v1's explicit acknowledgment that concurrent BWS work studied supervised double-end pruning, although the BWS citation remains elsewhere. These are targeted positioning changes rather than a replacement of the research context.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and substantially restructures its explanation around two challenges. It introduces a separate Preliminary section, reorganizes the methodology and ablations, expands explanatory passages, and replaces the numbered supplementary sections with Appendices A–D. Reproducibility, ethics, and limitations material is also redistributed and rewritten.

P2.justification: The overview and pipeline diagrams are redrawn, and the main performance presentation changes from curves and separate tables to an encoder-grouped table with colored cells. V2 adds several ablation tables and diagnostic figures, changes plot axes and styling, and reduces the class-wise error figure from six panels to four. The ImageNet example gallery is retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence for ELFS by isolating clustering and scoring choices, adding FreeSel and broader encoder-matched comparisons, and experimentally addressing the pretrained-model limitation. Clearer organization and reported code access further improve the paper. These gains outweigh the removed CINIC10 evaluation and detailed runtime breakdown. Overbroad superiority wording remains a weakness: v2 Table 1 reports 65.5% for ELFS versus 66.0% for D2 on CIFAR100 at 70% pruning with SwAV.
